facts.content: Patient experiences wheezing and shortness of breath for 2-3 days.
Patient has a cough.
Patient reports a 'fever' but measured temperature is 37°C.
Patient has dyspnea on exertion and can't walk to work.
Patient occasionally has difficulty finishing sentences due to shortness of breath.
Patient has no nocturnal symptoms.
Patient denies chest pain, sputum production, and hemoptysis.
Patient has a history of moderate to severe childhood asthma with intermittent hospital visits.
facts.source_text: PMH: Childhood asthma (moderate–severe; intermittent hospital visits, no ICU)

facts.content: Patient has a history of hay fever.
Patient has a history of eczema.
Patient uses Salbutamol inhaler as needed, every few weeks or before exercise.
facts.source_text: Meds: Salbutamol inhaler PRN (every few wks; before exercise)

facts.content: Patient takes no other medications.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Patient consumes alcohol at a rate of approximately 1 glass of wine every 2-3 days.
Patient lives with a partner and works as an engineer from home.
facts.source_text: lives with partner; engineer; WFH/sick leave due to SOB

facts.content: Assessment includes asthma exacerbation with symptoms of wheezing and shortness of breath lasting 2-3 days, a history of asthma, and the use of short-acting beta-agonists as needed.
facts.source_text: Asthma exacerbation: 2–3 days wheeze/SOB with cough; afebrile by measurement; hx asthma; using SABA PRN; DOE, occasional speech-limiting SOB

facts.content: Assessment includes allergic rhinitis likely acting as a contributing trigger.
facts.source_text: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever), contributing trigger likely

facts.content: History of eczema is part of the assessment.
Plan to increase short-acting beta-agonist to 2-4 puffs every 4 hours initially.
Prescribe and instruct on the use of a spacer.
facts.source_text: Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to instruct use

facts.content: Prescribe and instruct on the use of a peak flow meter, with morning and evening peak expiratory flow recording for 1 week.
facts.source_text: Prescribe peak flow meter; pharmacist to instruct; record PEF AM and PM x 1 week

facts.content: Provide safety net advice to call back urgently if there is increased wheezing, high fever, or worsening shortness of breath.
facts.source_text: Safety net: call back urgently if ↑wheeze, high fever, worsening SOB

facts.content: Arrange a review in approximately 1 week to assess control and consider adding a controller inhaler based on peak expiratory flow and symptoms.
facts.source_text: Arrange review in ~1 week to assess control; consider adding controller inhaler based on PEF/sx

facts.content: Plan includes starting regular over-the-counter antihistamine for allergic rhinitis.
facts.source_text: Start regular OTC antihistamine; add note with options

facts.content: Patient to have a phone or clinic review in 1 week, or sooner if symptoms worsen.
facts.source_text: Phone/clinic review in 1 week or sooner if worsening
